note: do(ʔ)aː parses as 'doa' (prayer), dʒaːdi as 'jadi', 'desa' and 'buram' clear. Words recover but the phrase makes no coherent sense; the long/glottal in 'doa' is slightly unnatural.
Plain [j] in 'ajam' heard as 'ayam' (chicken); 'daːn' = 'dan' (and). All words parse cleanly; meaning is a nonsensical list.

The double-r 'sar rumah' resolves to 'dasar rumah' (house foundation), clear. The opening 'haːli bu' does not parse; possibly a garbled 'ibu' (mother) buried in it, but a native ear does not land on a word.
'tanah', 'ibu', 'dalam', 'tiram' all parse instantly. Reads as a poetic (if odd) phrase; nothing forced.

gloss: earlier/just-now inside mind/character (or the name Budi)
note: 'tadi', 'dalam', 'budi' all parse. 'budi' is both a common noun (character/reason) and a personal name; either reading is native.
Weak glottal 'kitaːʔ ada' heard as 'kita ada'; 'malam' and 'rahim' clear. All words recover; sequence is not grammatical prose.
o̞ leans toward u, so 'ro̞sa' heard as 'rusa' (deer) rather than non-Indonesian 'rosa'; 'daːna' = 'dana' (fund). Words recover but stack into no meaning.
'rumah', 'sudah', 'rahim' all clean; a͡h sequences read naturally as final -h. Words fully recover, meaning surreal.
'tanah tadi dan kabut' parses instantly and is even loosely grammatical ('the earlier earth and the fog'). No friction.
Reduplicated 'tanah' plus 'rumah', all instant. Native reduplication pattern; fully recoverable.
